examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Packet store-and-forward begins forwarding after a full packet arrives, but links can pipeline consecutive packets. For N equal packets over k equal-rate links, negligible propagation gives (N+k−1) packet-transmission times. Circuit switching may have setup and reserved rate; do not substitute one model for the other.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Ten 1000-bit packets cross three 1 Mbps links with store-and-forward and negligible other delays. What total time is required in milliseconds?

**Answer: 12.** One packet takes 1 ms per link. The first reaches the destination after 3 ms; nine more arrive one per millisecond. Total=(10+3−1)·1=12 ms.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Sending one whole file as a single store-and-forward unit has a different fill cost from dividing it into packets.

A virtual circuit is not automatically a reserved-bandwidth circuit.
